# Time Series Analysis Basics

## Overview
Time series data is any data indexed by time, such as daily sales, hourly temperatures, or monthly website traffic, and it requires special handling because the order of observations matters and points close in time are related. A time series can be decomposed into components: a trend (long-term direction), seasonality (repeating patterns like weekday or holiday effects), and noise (random fluctuation). Pandas is excellent for this: with a DateTime index you can resample data to different frequencies (e.g., turn daily into monthly), compute rolling-window statistics like a 7-day moving average to smooth noise, and easily slice by date ranges. Two important concepts are stationarity (whether the statistical properties stay constant over time, which many forecasting methods assume) and autocorrelation (how a series correlates with its own past values). Even before advanced models, simple baselines, like predicting tomorrow equals today, or the average of the last week, are surprisingly effective and set the bar any fancier model must beat. Time series skills are essential for forecasting demand, finance, and operations.

## Deep Dive
This module covers: Time series components (trend, seasonality, noise); DateTime indexing and resampling in Pandas; Rolling windows and moving averages; Stationarity and autocorrelation; Simple forecasting baselines. Mastering these ideas is essential because they appear repeatedly in production AI systems.

### What You Will Learn
- The core theory behind today's topic.
- How to apply it using Python, NumPy, Pandas, or the relevant framework.
- How to evaluate results and avoid common mistakes.
- Where to find authoritative references when you need deeper detail.

### Real-World Context
In industry, these skills are used daily: data scientists clean messy survey data, AI engineers deploy models to REST APIs, and automation engineers orchestrate pipelines. Today's practical task simulates one of these real-world scenarios.

## Hands-On Practice
Practical Task: Load a time series dataset, set a DateTime index, resample it to a coarser frequency, plot a rolling moving average, and build a naive forecast baseline you evaluate against.
Mini Project: Build a time series analysis notebook that decomposes a real series into trend/seasonality/noise, visualizes rolling statistics, and compares two simple forecasting baselines with an error metric.
Assignment: Take a daily time series, compute 7-day and 30-day moving averages, and write an interpretation of the trend and any seasonality you observe.

Complete all three sections. Each completed section earns points toward your CalibiAI Score. If you are unsure about any part, use the AI assessment popup to submit your work and receive dynamic feedback from DeepSeek.

## Common Mistakes to Avoid
Many beginners rush into coding before fully understanding the data. Others skip validation steps and overestimate model performance. This module helps you build the discipline of checking assumptions first, then applying algorithms systematically.

## Career Impact
The skills covered today are frequently tested in technical interviews and required in entry-level AI engineering roles. Building a portfolio that demonstrates mastery of these concepts will significantly improve your job prospects.

## Key Takeaways
1. Theory guides practice — understand before coding.
2. Clean data and clear metrics are more valuable than complex models.
3. Document your steps for reproducibility.
4. Communication matters: explain results to non-technical stakeholders.
